newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine seeks foreign cash for gold sector.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine seeks foreign cash for gold sector.

text.p: Ukraine plans to court foreign investment to develop its fledgling gold industry, a top metals official said in an interview late on Thursday.
"The prospects for the gold industry here are not bad," said Mykola Havrylenko, head of the State Geology Committee.
"If we can attract investments, we could produce up to 15 tonnes of gold a year in a maximum of five years."
Ukraine is exploring three gold deposits in the Trans-Carpathian region in the west of the former Soviet republic, near the Hungarian border. Four mines are under construction.
Four deposits have also been discovered in the eastern region of Dnipropetrovsk, two in central Kirovohrad and one in the southern region of Odessa.

"We desperately need foreign money -- something between $600 and $800 million," Havrylenko said. "We need it to develop reserves, build new mines, buy equipment and also to develop gold-extraction plants."
He said that U.S., Canadian and Australian companies had shown some interest in investing, but gave no details.

He said the government did not plan to export gold in the near future, though the possibility could not be excluded in a few years. "We are not going to become the world's major gold producer anyway," he said.
The government is approving measures which will allow it to take a 51 percent stake in all companies set up to develop deposits and distributing mining licenses.
The rule would apply to Ukrzoloto -- the company which has been set up to identify and explore gold deposits -- and to future mining companies set up.
Havrylenko defended the need to keep a 51 percent stake in all gold enterprises but saw it as a temporary measure.
"Now we are at the first stage of goldmining and the state must have control over the industry," he said.
"But in the future the governmental stake will be reduced step by step to....a role of supervisor."
Interfax-Ukraine news agency quoted government sources as saying on Friday that Ukrzoloto wanted to set up a joint stock company, Ukraine Gold International.
It said that international investors would have a chance to buy stakes in six to 18 months after the company was created.
Industry Minister Valery Mazur has said Ukraine will produce its first gold next year, forecasting output of 900 kilograms.
Ukraine's untapped reserves of precious metals like gold are far below levels seen in Russia and Kazakhstan.
